messages:
Alex: heads up — after the kernel-selector tweak we rolled yesterday, decode tail latency jumped on small-chat workloads. 95p from 90ms -> 220ms on a few pods.
Maya: ugh. seeing it in the dashboard too. can you paste the perf profile?
Alex: attached flamegraph from prof-run-1748: lots of time in kernel fallback paths and small-batch kernel path. interestingly prefill batch sizes are fine, decode batch sizes collapsed to 1-2 tokens per request.
Devon: that smells like token-budget math or queue policy. if decode is allowed to preempt prefill incorrectly you'll get tiny decode batches and KV cache churn.
Maya: KV cache churn? explain quick.
Devon: when decode batches are tiny and interleaved, they repeatedly touch KV cache (small prefixes) and push the working set out. then following prefill misses force recompute and latency spikes.
Priya: i ran the kv-hit-rate probe — decode-heavy traces show hit-rate drop from 98% -> 73% during the spike window. correlates.
Alex: timeline: kernel selector change introduced a heavier weight for 'lowest-p50' which favored a different kernel for short sequences. that kernel has worse throughput for many tiny decode batches in our scheduling topology.
Maya: so two orthogonal problems: selector picks a slower kernel for tiny decodes, and batching heuristic allows too many tiny decode batches (token budget / age flush wrong).
Devon: propose quick mitigations: 1) emergency revert selector weight for short-seq until we have a perf test. 2) enforce min-decode-batch-tokens=8 (config) so scheduler accumulates a few tokens before flush unless age>10ms.
Priya: +1. also suggest separate logical queues: prefill-q and decode-q with different token_budget targets and fairness tokens. decode-q should have a slightly lower priority but higher min_tokens to avoid starving prefill.
Alex: rough config snippet i tested locally: 
```
queue.policies = [
  {name: "prefill", token_target: 128, min_tokens: 16, age_ms: 8},
  {name: "decode",  token_target: 64,  min_tokens: 8,  age_ms: 6, priority: 0.8}
]
kernel.selector.short_seq_penalty = 0.7  # bias away from tiny-decode-unfriendly kernels
```
Maya: nice. what about KV drain? any gating there?
Devon: add a cache-preserve window: if a request touches KV for a given key, give that context a small grace period where we prefer not to evict its blocks. effectively a tiny LRU boost for hot contexts. cheap and reduces recompute.
Priya: the perf harness shows that combined changes (min_tokens + kernel bias + kv-grace) bring 95p decode down to ~95ms and restore kv-hit to 96%. full numbers in the run artifact.
Alex: can we canary these changes to 10% of runtime pods? also need A/B of selector-revert vs kernel-bias param (to avoid full revert).
Maya: plan: create canary rollout, run real-chat workload for 4h, watch 95/99 latencies and kv-hit. if stable, promote.
Devon: i'll own the scheduler config push and add metrics: effective_tokens_per_batch, avg_batch_wait_ms, kv_hit_by_context.
Priya: i'll add an automated alert for kv-hit-rate < 90% for more than 1m, and a regression test in perf-suite that simulates interleaved prefill/decode.
Alex: @perf-bot please schedule perf-run on canary after rollout and post results here.
perf-bot: scheduled perf-run 1757503200 -> artifact://runs/1757503200.json :eyes:
Maya: thanks. timeline?
Devon: aiming to stage canary this afternoon (ET), monitor for 6h, then decide. posting rollout PR in ~20m.
Alex: 👍 keep thread updated. if anyone sees weird KV evictions / OOMs ping me directly.
Priya: putting checklist in the PR: backout steps, metrics dashboard links, perf artifacts.
Maya: sounds good. small follow-up — we should add a unit test for kernel-selector that asserts won’t pick tiny-decode-unfriendly kernel when avg_decode_length<12.
Devon: will add test. done.
Alex: ok closing loop — thanks team.
